record.summary: Announcement of a new U.S. AI Safety Institute, led by the National Institute of Standards and Technology in the Department of Commerce, as part of NIST's response to Executive Order 14110. The institute was to build on the AI Risk Management Framework to improve organizations' ability to evaluate and validate AI systems, partner with other agencies on evaluating AI capabilities, limitations, risks and impacts and on building testbeds, and work with ally and partner countries to share best practices and align capability evaluation and red-team guidance and benchmarks. An AI Safety Institute Consortium supports its work.
record.notes: Announced on 1 November 2023 at the UK's AI Safety Summit 2023, in which Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo took part, as part of NIST's response to Executive Order 14110 (US-04). On 2 November 2023 NIST called for participants in the AI Safety Institute Consortium, a core element of the institute. The Commerce Secretary's statement of 3 June 2025 transformed the institute into the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) within NIST (US-15). By October 2026 NIST presents the center as the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (CAISSI).

These are other NIST documents, not the press release, so they count at most as alt-official evidence. The White House fact sheet of 1 Nov 2023 could not be stored (DNS lookup failed). The summary now follows NIST's description of the institute; version 1's 'lead federal AI safety work', 'standards for authenticating AI-generated content' and 'allied safety institutes such as the UK's' are not in a stored file and were dropped, and the topic 'general-purpose / frontier AI' was removed for the same reason.

summary.quote: This consortium is a core element of the new NIST-led U.S. AI Safety Institute announced yesterday at the U.K.’s AI Safety Summit 2023, in which U.S. Secretary of Commerce Gina Raimondo participated.
The institute and its consortium are part of NIST’s response to the recently released Executive Order on Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of AI.
The institute aims to measurably improve organizations’ ability to evaluate and validate AI systems, as detailed in the AI RMF Roadmap.
The U.S. AI Safety Institute will harness work already underway by NIST and others to build the foundation for trustworthy AI systems, supporting use of the AI RMF
The U.S. AI Safety Institute will partner with other U.S. government agencies on evaluating AI capabilities, limitations, risks and impacts and coordinate on building testbeds.
The institute will also work with organizations in ally and partner countries to share best practices, align capability evaluation, and red-team guidance and benchmarks.

judgment.status_reasoning: NIST's CAISI evaluation report (September 2025) cites the Commerce Secretary's 'Statement ... on Transforming the U.S. AI Safety Institute into the Pro-Innovation, Pro-Science U.S. Center for AI Standards and Innovation' and dates his tasking of CAISI to 3 June 2025. The institute this announcement created was replaced by CAISI (record US-15), so 'Superseded' stands.
judgment.date_reasoning: NIST's news release is dated 2 November 2023 ('Released November 2, 2023') and says the institute was 'announced yesterday', which gives 1 November 2023, the published value. date_last_updated 2025-06-03 is the date of the Commerce Secretary's statement transforming the institute into CAISI, as the CAISI report gives it.
judgment.scope_reasoning: The founding mandate of a national AI safety institute; in scope with no note.
